brief: Gift baskets, pears, and holiday food gifts, $40-150. Q4 is basically our whole year. Looking for people who give gifts (corporate, family, hosts).

profile.business_summary: A seasonal DTC brand specializing in premium gift baskets, pears, and holiday food gifts ranging from $40 to $150, with a heavy sales concentration in Q4. They target corporate, family, and host gift-givers.

profile.fulfillment_notes: Highly seasonal business with peak operations and sales concentrated in Q4.

relevant_tags.why: The brand's primary value proposition is holiday, corporate, and host gift-giving.
Holiday food gifts and gift baskets typically contain shelf-stable pantry items.
They sell physical food products, specifically pears and food baskets.
Gifts for hosts are frequently home-oriented or consumed in hosting environments.

note_signals.why: Strong gifting season uplift in Nov-Dec perfectly matches the advertiser's Q4-dominant sales cycle.
Older affluent audience with high AOV is an ideal demographic for premium holiday and family gift baskets.
Highest-AOV publisher with conservative brand sensibility aligns well with premium corporate and holiday gifting.
Kitchen and home audience motivated by gifting and hosting events aligns with holiday food gifts.
Late-night, high-frequency, impulse-driven convenience purchases do not align with planned $40-150 holiday gift purchases.

profile.gate_reason: The product, price point, target audience, and seasonal focus are clearly defined, allowing for immediate campaign planning.

config.advertiser_summary: A seasonal DTC brand specializing in premium gift baskets, pears, and holiday food gifts ranging from $40 to $150, with a heavy sales concentration in Q4. They target corporate, family, and host gift-givers.

assumptions: No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 40% gross margin (typical for groceries). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($95 x 40% margin x 1.0 orders = $38.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $26.60 x click-to-purchase rate (1.6%-5.6% for groceries). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.24 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.19 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.24 -> relative fit x1.39 on CTR/CVR; max bid $1.18 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $840, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $26.60 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
